findings.evidence: Template rows such as "| `buzz` | 2 | X, X everywhere |", "| `success` | 2 | A confirmed win |" and "| `mordor` | 2 | \"One does not simply...\" |" restate meme meanings the model already knows
findings.fix: Keep the expert columns (verified ID and line count) and the non-obvious notes (fry for unconfirmed outcomes, cmm one line only, db needs a hand-built URL). Cut the 'Use for' text to a 1-3 word name for the well-known memes.

findings.evidence: "4. **Write the joke:** name the contrast, write the payoff (last line) first, then the setup. Keep each line to about 6 words."
findings.fix: Make step 4 a short decision framework. Before writing, ask: who will see it (team Slack, public post, PR), who the butt of the joke is (never a named teammate or customer), and which line count the joke really needs. Then pick the template from that answer, not from a keyword.

findings.evidence: "**Never say a deploy or test run succeeded unless the user confirmed it.** Use `fry` while the outcome is unknown." gives no reason, unlike the other gotchas
findings.fix: Add the reason: a meme posted to Slack or a PR is read as a status report, so a premature 'success' meme can tell the team that a broken release is fine.

findings.evidence: The queries are short and context-free, for example "make a meme with custom top and bottom text for Slack" and "create a logo for our developer team". None has a file path, an image URL, personal backstory or a typo, and the hardest positive (captions on a user-supplied image URL, template custom) is missing.
findings.fix: Rewrite 5-6 queries with realistic context: casual typos, a concrete image URL to caption (should trigger), a pasted incident summary that asks for 'something funny for #eng-random' without saying 'meme' (should trigger), and a near-miss negative that asks to caption a local photo.jpg with no URL.

findings.evidence: Step 6 requires "a Markdown image whose alt text describes both the picture and the joke", but the `--markdown` flag in step 5 calls get_markdown_image(url) with no alt argument, so scripts/meme_generator.py always prints ![Meme](...)
findings.fix: Add `--alt TEXT` to the generate subparser and pass it to get_markdown_image. Until then, tell the agent in step 5 to drop `--markdown` and write `![<picture and joke>](<url>)` itself.

findings.evidence: "`python3 scripts/meme_generator.py suggest \"<situation>\"`" does not mention the script's top-level `--json` flag, which argparse only accepts before the subcommand (`--json suggest ...`)
findings.fix: Document `python3 scripts/meme_generator.py --json suggest "<situation>"` and `--json list-templates`, and note that `--json` must come before the subcommand.

findings.evidence: "If a line would wrap past two rows or get cropped, shorten it and regenerate once." An agent that cannot view the image cannot check this.
findings.fix: Give a checkable proxy, for example: if any caption line is over about 30 characters (about 20 for 3-line templates), shorten it before building the URL. Check the render visually only when you can view images.

findings.evidence: "make a meme about bugs everywhere in our release" exemplifies the positive queries: all explicitly name memes, greentext, memegen.link or a template. None tests the description's implicit reaction-image or image-URL captioning triggers, and none supplies a custom background URL.
findings.fix: Replace two explicit positives with realistic implicit requests: a contextual Slack comparison-image request without the word 'meme', and a request to caption a supplied public image URL at specified dimensions. Keep the balanced positive/negative set and existing near-miss negatives.

findings.evidence: "No Python? Send POST https://api.memegen.link/images with JSON {\"template_id\": \"<id>\", \"text\": [\"<top>\", \"<bottom>\"]}" omits the selected background and rendering options. Following this fallback for the advertised custom-image branch loses the user's background instead of producing the requested image.
findings.fix: Route no-Python requests through the documented hand-built URL procedure, preserving one path segment per caption and all selected query parameters. Explicitly require the percent-encoded background parameter for custom images and preserve width, height, layout, font and style when supplied.
